name: Medium Green
lede: Medium Green names itself: a plain mid-saturation [[green]], filed under the ISCC-NBS 1955 lists and later picked up by the xkcd color survey.

sections.title: A modifier, twice over
sections.body:
The name is ordinary modifier grammar, "medium" plus the parent hue [[green]] [1]. Our library's earliest record for it is the ISCC-NBS 1955 lists, in color block 151, and the xkcd color survey later used the same words for a brighter, more saturated green [1]. Neither source explains the name beyond the two plain words [1].

Its nearest named neighbors by measured color are [[shamrock]] and [[peppermint]], a touch brighter and duller respectively, with [[green-pigment|Green (pigment)]] close behind [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive carries a close match to this exact shade of green, covering at least one percent of its canvas, as photographed [2]. That says something about this archive and its mix of museums and periods, not about painting as a whole, and not about how often the color turns up anywhere else [2]. Greens this saturated and this specific a lightness are harder for any photograph of an aged, varnished canvas to hold onto than a duller, darker green [2].
